description: Query a published authority on the NOMOS Exchange marketplace — a different system from verify_decision's own sealed policies. Every public authority (e.g. eu-ai-act.nomos) is queryable with no key. Returns the authority's own verdict (AUTHORIZED/DENIED/ESCALATED), the exact rule and reason, and a permanent, cryptographically-bound transcript (query_id + url) — replayable evidence, not just a reply. Nothing is invented or paraphrased: the verdict is the authority's sealed rules evaluated against your inputs. The default response is a short, curated summary (verdict, matched rule, source citation when the artifact has one, transparency/completeness disclosures, transcript link) — not the full rule-by-rule evaluation trace. Set include_evaluation_trace: true to get that complete diagnostic record when you or the user actually need it.

action.description: Optional label for what this query represents, for the caller's own transcript record (e.g. "pre-deployment check"). Purely descriptive — does not affect the verdict.

acts_for.description: Optional organisation the agent acts for. Recorded as declared; when an Exchange key is used, the key's account is recorded instead.

agent_id.description: Optional stable name for the agent asking (e.g. "acme-credit-agent"). Recorded on the transcript and shown in the authority's public history as who relies on it.

authority.description: The Exchange artifact's standard name — its short slug, optionally ".nomos"-suffixed (e.g. "eu-ai-act" or "eu-ai-act.nomos"), or its raw artifact ID. Browse the catalog at https://www.nomosprotocol.com/exchange.

exchange_api_key.description: Exchange API key (nxk_...). Optional for free/public queries. Required only for metered access to licensed (paid) authorities beyond their free allotment.

include_evaluation_trace.description: Set true to receive the full rule-by-rule evaluation trace (every rule checked, every missing field) instead of the default curated summary. Most callers never need this.

inputs.description: Key/value facts to evaluate against the authority's rules (e.g. {"ai_categorises_biometric_data_for_sensitive_attributes": true}). Fields must match the authority's vocabulary — see the atlas endpoint or the artifact's catalog page.

purpose.description: Set "test" for test or evaluation queries: they are answered and sealed, but kept out of the authority's public history and counts. Defaults to production.

name: ask_authority

expected_fields.description: Present only when ESCALATED for lack of data — the fields this authority still needs

matched_rule_id.description: ID of the rule that determined the verdict — null when AUTHORIZED with no matching rule

matched_rule_name.description: Human-readable name/description of the matched rule — use this for display, not matched_rule_id

open_higher_priority_count.description: 0 means every relevant fact was known when this was sealed; >0 means facts were still missing above the matched rule

open_higher_priority_rules.description: The actual rules behind open_higher_priority_count (capped to 20) — use this to answer "which ones?" instead of guessing. Each has the rule name, what it would do if it matched, and exactly which input fields are missing.

query_id.description: Permanent transcript ID — reopen any time at the returned url

response_source.description: Provenance label — this is a sealed NOMOS verdict, not Claude's own reasoning. Preserve or restate this distinction when relaying the answer.

rules_evaluated.description: Only present when include_evaluation_trace was true

rules_evaluated_count.description: Total rules checked during evaluation — the size of the full trace, whether or not it was returned

source_reference.description: Citation for the matched rule, when the source document's structure was captured at extraction time. Names where the rule TEXT was extracted from (e.g. "Article 5"), not a legal claim about what it covers. Null if unavailable.

url.description: Path to the permanent, shareable transcript for this query

verdict_description.description: Human-readable reason — the exact rule and its consequence
